author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A judge has allowed attorneys for the family of Massachusetts State Trooper Kevin Trainor to attach a restaurant owner’s home and liquor license as security while their civil lawsuit proceeds.

The family is seeking $20 million from Tribu, a Saugus restaurant, after Trainor was killed in a wrong-way collision on Route 1 in May. Plaintiffs allege the driver was served nine drinks at the restaurant before leaving and striking Trainor’s vehicle. Those claims have not been resolved at trial.

At Tuesday’s Essex County Superior Court hearing, lawyers for the restaurant argued that the $20 million estimate was arbitrary and disputed whether the plaintiffs were likely to recover that amount. The judge nevertheless approved the requested attachments in place of insurance, Boston 25 News reported.

The decision does not determine liability or damages. It preserves identified assets while the parties begin discovery and litigate the underlying allegations. The Massachusetts Alcoholic Beverages Control Commission said it was still reviewing Tribu’s liquor license, which remained active at the time of the report.
dek: The ruling permits plaintiffs to attach a restaurant owner’s home and liquor license while a $20 million civil case moves into discovery.
headline: Judge allows asset attachments in Trooper Trainor family lawsuit
